newsitem.title: USA: Thomson cuts satellite dish prices.
newsitem.headline: Thomson cuts satellite dish prices.

text.p: Thomson Consumer Electronics confirmed on Monday that it will cut the prices of its small digital satellite system (DSS) receiver dishes to $399 from $599, effective August 29.
In addition to the price cut, DIRECTV, a unit of Hughes Electronics Corp, which provides programming for the satellite systems, will offer a rebate of $200, dropping the price of the dishes to $199.
Thomson said the new price, combined with the rebate should in part result in annual sales of 2.3 million units, 500,000 more than previously expected.
Thomson said it will expand its manufacturing capacity for DSS with a fifth production line later this year. The company said it began the making the systems in 1994 with two lines.
Thomson manufactures RCA, GE and ProScan brands of consumer electronic products. It expects the three brands to account for seven out of 10 DSS systems sold in the United States this year.
To get the DIRECTV rebate, available through December 31, buyers must purchase a one-year subscription of DIRECTV programming, Thomson said.

In addition, U.S. Satellite Broadcasting System, which also provides programming, said it had extended a program giving buyers of any 18-inch DSS dish $200 in coupons, including discounts on programming.
